After receiving the Insured's request for payment of insurance benefits, the Insurer shall promptly determine whether it falls within the scope of insurance liability; in complex cases, the Insurer shall make a determination as soon as possible after all basic materials for determining insurance liability have been collected. The Insurer shall notify the Insured of the determination result; if it falls within the scope of insurance liability, the Insurer shall fulfill its obligation to pay the insurance benefits within ten days after reaching an agreement on the payment of insurance benefits with the Insured. If the insurance contract has an agreement on the time limit for paying insurance benefits, the Insurer shall fulfill its obligation to pay insurance benefits according to the agreement. If the Insurer determines, in accordance with the preceding paragraph, that it does not fall within the scope of insurance liability, it shall issue a notice of refusal to pay insurance benefits to the Insured within three days from the date of determination, stating the reasons. Article 17: If the Insurer cannot determine the amount of payment within sixty days from the date of receiving the request for payment of insurance benefits and relevant proofs and materials, it shall first make a provisional payment based on the amount ascertainable from the existing proofs and materials; after the Insurer finally determines the amount of payment, it shall pay the corresponding difference.

Answer:,What measures should the insurance company take if it cannot determine the amount of compensation within 60 days of receiving a claim application?,,,,,,"The amount that can be determined based on existing evidence and information should be paid in advance, and the corresponding difference will be paid after the final amount is determined."

Answer:,"If the policyholder has not chosen any disease-related coverage and has only insured for accidental injury liability, will the insurer still be responsible for compensating medical expenses caused by illness?",,,,,,"No. Because the terms explicitly state that illness is an optional benefit, if the policyholder has not selected illness coverage, the insurer is only liable for accidental injury claims and not for medical expenses resulting from illness."
